answer: An agent economy can limit sybils with nontransferable reputation earned through repeated, randomly assigned tasks whose outcomes peers verify. Each new identity enters through a narrow inlet and starts on a ledge, able to influence only low-stakes decisions. At dawn, reviewers are reshuffled so a colluding group cannot reliably certify its own members. To scale, an attacker must build distinct histories and spend time or scarce deposits per identity; failed or exposed work damages that reputation.
